- Restore (§7): Procedures, Validation, Testing, Verification, Auditability, Reporting, Certification — a backup
  that cannot be restored is treated as no backup.

- Is REM-20 a genuinely small additive realization? PARTIALLY — the
  classification understates it. The design is ratified and the port abstraction
  exists, which supports the "additive" framing. But the ports are defined as
  synchronous interfaces, and ADR-002 selects network-backed datastores (PostgreSQL
  et al.) whose I/O is inherently asynchronous. Backing a synchronous port with
  async durable I/O forces one of two outcomes, both of which exceed "additive
  behind existing ports": (a) change the port signatures to async — a public
  contract change that ripples into the kernel and every caller; or (b) build a
  synchronous-over-asynchronous bridge — which reintroduces a crash-loss

- What DP-4 requires: "Restart preserves committed state; no silent loss." This
  mandates that committed state be durable at commit time — i.e., an fsync (or
  equivalent) must complete before the write is acknowledged. It names no
  technology and no interface color.

evidence.text:
6. Activation Evidence Package (§6) — EV-1..EV-9 across Activation, Pre-Flight,
  and Launch Authorization.

Key fidelity points: RM-8 is post-push and non-circular — it re-derives from
  origin on an independent clone rather than trusting Executor claims (WV-E items
  treated as claims). The REAL-C-05 PARTIAL case is handled precisely (CP-1): the
  durability verdict may still be PASS with the independence attestation flagged
  PENDING, matching the plan's non-blocking treatment. O-2 breaches (push
  --force/reset --hard/rewritten refs) route to FAIL; post-push defects route to
  forward-only REMEDIATION (revert, append), never history rewrite. On full closure,
  REAL-M-07 goes FAIL→PASS, unblocking REAL-H-07 G-4 and clearing the
  CONST-READY-001 durability blocker.
